subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-099.turn2.draft.md
summary: Turn 2 places the full fleet-class contract in its own bytes, preserves the five D-006 startup gates and weekly-roll regression rule, and removes both `/proc/self/exe` and fat-slice ambiguity. The accepted target-process repair is still incomplete, however. The prose states a same-PID exec sequence but supplies no actual exec-completion handshake, and a pipe cannot by itself keep an arbitrary post-exec help/version target alive. On macOS it says translation is read from the child after exec without defining a target self-report or target-PID API; `sysctl.proc_translated` reports the calling process. The dispatch provenance table also presents both the historical pre-D-098 and current post-D-098 COORD hashes under the same `COORD` label while calling every row a turn-2 dispatch input. These two SHOULD-FIX defects prohibit CONSENT and the proposed condition-4 MET transition.

objections.title: The stated same-PID sequence still lacks an executable post-exec sampling protocol
objections.finding: Lines 127-142 improve target identity substantially, but `fork`, record T, then `execve` is a sequence, not an exec-completion handshake. The parent is not told how it distinguishes the pre-exec child/helper from the successfully exec'd target. The sentence that a short command 'is held live with a pipe' supplies no pipe endpoints or target behavior: a close-on-exec pipe can notify a parent that exec occurred, but does not keep the new image alive; redirecting output to a pipe does not guarantee blocking for bounded help/version output. Thus `/proc/T/exe` and `proc_pidpath(T)` can be sampled before exec or after exit. On macOS, the draft additionally says `sysctl.proc_translated` is read from the child after exec but defines no target command/self-report and no target-PID API. Apple's documented sysctl call reports the calling process, so a parent cannot obtain T's value merely by naming T. `file` of `proc_pidpath(T)` remains executable metadata and does not fill that missing target translation observation.
evidence: D-099 turn 2 lines 130-142 name fork/exec, a live PID, and a pipe but specify no close-on-exec success/error channel, wait/stop state, process start identity, target cooperation, or exact sampling API/output.
The governed target commands are `--help` and `--version` with bounded startup latency (lines 59-63), so unsynchronized post-exec inspection has a direct exit race.
Linux procfs identifies `/proc/<pid>/exe` as the executable link and warns that PIDs may be reused after exit: https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.8/filesystems/proc.html .

Apple documents `sysctl.proc_translated` as a call made by the process whose translation state is being tested: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/Apple-Silicon/about-the-rosetta-translation-environment .
objections.impact: The harness can sample the launcher, fail nondeterministically after a fast target exits, or lack any lawful way to obtain the macOS target's Rosetta state. The contract therefore still cannot reproduce its claimed independent host/executable/live-process facts fail closed.
objections.requiredRepair: Define an actual per-OS protocol. Establish successful exec and exact target identity with a specified handshake, bind PID plus start identity to the digest-pinned path, and stop or cooperatively block the post-exec target until all observations complete. A pipe is sufficient only if the target has an expressly defined read/write protocol after exec; otherwise name a documented stopped-after-exec primitive. Specify the exact Linux process-ABI observation rather than counting executable `file` output twice. On macOS require an exact target-PID API and field or an implemented target self-report that calls `sysctl.proc_translated` inside T, with normalized values and error behavior. Refreeze for turn 3.

objections.title: The turn-2 dispatch table conflates historical and current COORD inputs
objections.finding: The section is titled 'Measured inputs at turn-2 dispatch', yet line 253 labels COORD as `17262fe0...` and line 264 labels COORD again as `09840050...`. The live file at this dispatch is only `09840050...`; `17262fe0...` is the historical COORD state at D-097 / before the C-D098 record. The adjacent generic `turn-1 subject`, `turn-2 subject`, and reviewer labels likewise first refer to D-098 and later refer to D-099 without a decision prefix. The underlying historical hashes are reproducible, but the table's single dispatch scope makes two different bytes appear simultaneously current and leaves replay consumers unable to tell which decision each generic row belongs to.
evidence: D-099 turn 2 lines 249-267 contain two `COORD` rows with different digests and duplicate generic turn/reviewer labels under one turn-2-dispatch heading.

The COORD object at D-097 commit 11691723d2a4b959daf9ddf5ac3df3977f8259ac is 17262fe0d40b8a41fae8d5391691809eb436102b842118652e042695ee749326; the object at C-D098 / current HEAD 09d0e288509f8b3e58d035290ff26f2e1d29c4ce is 0984005085b96920c2b4d3d561e950853bd40b6d97ee2cac77e457d647fe301b.
objections.impact: The frozen provenance recital is internally ambiguous about current versus inherited historical evidence, defeating the instruction to remeasure a cited file when it moves and making automated or human replay prone to selecting the stale COORD state.
objections.requiredRepair: Split the table into explicitly labeled `D-098 historical inputs` and `D-099 turn-2 dispatch inputs`, prefix every turn subject/verdict row with its decision and turn, and identify the commit/object for historical file hashes. Under the current-dispatch table, retain exactly one COORD row at the live digest. Refreeze for turn 3.
